questions.question_hindi: संविधान के अनुच्छेद 29(1) के अंतर्गत भारत के क्षेत्र या उसके किसी भाग में रहने वाले नागरिकों के ऐसे वर्ग को, जिसकी अपनी विशिष्ट भाषा, लिपि या संस्कृति है, कौन-सा अधिकार प्राप्त है?
options_hindi: उसे क्षेत्र के अन्य समुदायों पर अनिवार्य रूप से लागू करना।
अलग राज्य शिक्षा बोर्ड स्थापित करना।
उसके प्रचार के लिए विशेष केंद्रीय वित्तपोषण प्राप्त करना।

questions.subject: UPSC Principal Paper
questions.question_english: Under Article 29(1) of the Constitution, any section of the citizens residing in the territory of India or any part thereof having a distinct language, script or culture of its own shall have the right to:
options_english: Impose it on other communities in their region
Establish a separate state board of education
Receive exclusive central funding for its promotion
questions.explanation_english: Article 29(1) guarantees that any section of citizens residing in India possessing a distinct language, script, or culture has the fundamental right to conserve the same. This cultural guarantee enables linguistic and cultural groups to take all necessary institutional and educational steps to preserve their distinct heritage without arbitrary state interference or forced assimilation into the surrounding regional culture.
questions.explanation_hindi: सही उत्तर A है। अनुच्छेद 29(1) किसी विशिष्ट भाषा, लिपि या संस्कृति वाले नागरिकों के वर्ग को उसका संरक्षण करने का अधिकार देता है। यह सांस्कृतिक अधिकार है; इससे उस वर्ग को अपनी भाषा या संस्कृति अन्य समुदायों पर थोपने का अधिकार नहीं मिलता और न ही अलग शिक्षा बोर्ड या विशेष केंद्रीय वित्तपोषण स्वतः सुनिश्चित होता है।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (A) Conserve the same

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: Article 29(1) guarantees that any section of citizens residing in India possessing a distinct language, script, or culture has the fundamental right to conserve the same. This cultural guarantee enables linguistic and cultural groups to take all necessary institutional and educational steps to preserve their distinct heritage without arbitrary state interference or forced assimilation into the surrounding regional culture.

questions.question_hindi:
उन्नीकृष्णन निर्णय (1993) के संबंध में निम्नलिखित कथनों पर विचार कीजिए:
I. इसने प्रारंभिक शिक्षा के अधिकार और उच्च शिक्षा के अधिकार के बीच अंतर स्पष्ट किया।
II. इसने घोषित किया कि उच्च शिक्षा मौलिक अधिकार नहीं है।
III. इसने निजी व्यावसायिक महाविद्यालयों में प्रवेश और शुल्क को विनियमित करने की योजना स्थापित की।
कौन-से कथन सही हैं?
questions.source: AI-generated from supplied reference material; Constitutional Provisions Related to Education
questions.subject: UPSC Principal Paper
questions.question_english:
Consider these statements regarding the Unni Krishnan judgment (1993):
I. It explicitly separated the right to elementary education from the right to higher education.
II. It declared that higher education is not a fundamental right.
III. It established the scheme for regulating admissions and fee structures in private professional colleges. 
Which of the above statements are correct?
questions.explanation_english: In Unni Krishnan (1993), the Supreme Court separated elementary education (a fundamental right up to age 14) from higher education (which is subject to economic capacity). The Court created a detailed regulatory scheme for professional college admissions and fee structures to curb commercialization, making all three statements correct.
questions.explanation_hindi: सही उत्तर D है। उन्नीकृष्णन निर्णय ने 14 वर्ष तक की शिक्षा को मौलिक अधिकार के रूप में और उच्च शिक्षा को राज्य की आर्थिक क्षमता के अधीन समझने का ढाँचा दिया। इसने निजी व्यावसायिक संस्थानों में प्रवेश और शुल्क विनियमन के लिए एक योजना भी स्थापित की। इसलिए तीनों कथन निर्णय के मुख्य परिणामों का वर्णन करते हैं, जैसा स्रोत की उत्तर-व्याख्या में दिया गया है।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (D) I, II and III

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: In Unni Krishnan (1993), the Supreme Court separated elementary education (a fundamental right up to age 14) from higher education (which is subject to economic capacity). The Court created a detailed regulatory scheme for professional college admissions and fee structures to curb commercialization, making all three statements correct.

questions.question_hindi: दिल्ली का एक मान्यता-प्राप्त निजी गैर-सहायता प्राप्त विद्यालय RTE अधिनियम के 25% EWS/DG कोटे से बचने के लिए धार्मिक आधार पर अल्पसंख्यक दर्जे का दावा करता है। इस दावे की संवैधानिक स्थिति क्या है?
options_hindi: सरकारी भूमि पर चलने के कारण गैर-सहायता प्राप्त अल्पसंख्यक विद्यालयों को भी 25% कोटा लागू करना होगा।
केवल सहायता-प्राप्त अल्पसंख्यक विद्यालयों को छूट है।
बिना किसी अपवाद के सभी निजी विद्यालयों को 25% कोटा लागू करना होगा।
गैर-सहायता प्राप्त अल्पसंख्यक विद्यालयों को RTE के 25% EWS आरक्षण आदेश से छूट है।
questions.source: AI-generated from supplied reference material; Constitutional Provisions Related to Education
questions.subject: UPSC Principal Paper
questions.question_english: Read the situation below and answer the question that follows: A recognized private unaided school in Delhi claims minority status based on religion to avoid implementing the 25% EWS/DG quota mandated by the RTE Act. What is the constitutionally correct position regarding this claim?
options_english: Unaided minority schools must fulfill the 25% quota as they operate on land allotted by the government.
Only aided minority schools are exempt from the RTE mandate.
All private schools, without exception, must implement the 25% quota under Article 21A.
Unaided minority schools are exempt from the RTE mandate of 25% EWS reservation.
questions.explanation_english: In Pramati Educational and Cultural Trust (2014), the Supreme Court held that the RTE Act, including its mandatory 25% EWS quota, does not apply to minority educational institutions (both aided and unaided) covered under Article 30(1), as enforcing it would infringe upon constitutional rights granted to minorities.
questions.explanation_hindi: सही उत्तर D है। प्रमती एजुकेशनल एंड कल्चरल ट्रस्ट (2014) निर्णय के अनुसार RTE अधिनियम का 25% EWS कोटा अनुच्छेद 30(1) के अंतर्गत संरक्षित अल्पसंख्यक शैक्षणिक संस्थानों पर लागू नहीं होता। इसलिए यदि विद्यालय विधिसम्मत रूप से अल्पसंख्यक संस्थान है, तो केवल RTE अधिनियम के इस कोटे के आधार पर उसे गैर-अल्पसंख्यक निजी विद्यालय जैसा दायित्व नहीं दिया जा सकता। यह निष्कर्ष संस्थान के वास्तविक अल्पसंख्यक दर्जे और लागू कानूनी स्थिति पर निर्भर करेगा।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (D) Unaided minority schools are exempt from the RTE mandate of 25% EWS reservation.

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: In Pramati Educational and Cultural Trust (2014), the Supreme Court held that the RTE Act, including its mandatory 25% EWS quota, does not apply to minority educational institutions (both aided and unaided) covered under Article 30(1), as enforcing it would infringe upon constitutional rights granted to minorities.

कारण (R): सर्वोच्च न्यायालय ने सूचना जानने के अधिकार को संविधान के अनुच्छेद 19(1)(क), अर्थात् वाक् और अभिव्यक्ति की स्वतंत्रता, से अंतर्निहित माना है।
सही विकल्प चुनिए।

A और R दोनों सही हैं, लेकिन R, A की सही व्याख्या नहीं है।

Consider the following Assertion (A) and Reason (R).
Assertion (A): The Right to Information (RTI) Act is heavily utilized by parents to access school records and admission criteria.
Reason (R): The Supreme Court has held that the right to information is implicitly guaranteed by Article 19(1)(a) (freedom of speech and expression) of the Constitution.
options_english: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false

questions.explanation_english: The Supreme Court held in State of UP v. Raj Narain and subsequent cases that the right to know and access public information is derived from freedom of speech and expression under Article 19(1)(a). key_facts: Printed answer key: (A) Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: The Supreme Court held in State of UP v. Raj Narain and subsequent cases that the right to know and access public information is derived from freedom of speech and expression under Article 19(1)(a). The RTI Act operationalizes this fundamental right, making the reason a direct explanation.

questions.question_hindi: किस संविधान संशोधन ने अनुच्छेद 30(1क) जोड़ा, ताकि अल्पसंख्यक शैक्षणिक संस्थान की संपत्ति के अनिवार्य अधिग्रहण से अनुच्छेद 30(1) के अधिकार का हनन न हो?
questions.source: AI-generated from supplied reference material; Constitutional Provisions Related to Education

questions.question_english: Which Constitutional Amendment inserted Article 30(1A) to ensure that the compulsory acquisition of property of a minority educational institution does not abrogate the right guaranteed under Article 30(1)?
questions.explanation_english: The 44th Constitutional Amendment Act of 1978 inserted Article 30(1A) into the Constitution. When the right to property was removed as a fundamental right, this amendment ensured that compulsory acquisition of property belonging to a minority educational institution requires state compensation at rates that do not restrict or abrogate the fundamental right guaranteed under Article 30(1) of the Constitution.
questions.explanation_hindi: सही उत्तर 44वाँ संविधान संशोधन अधिनियम, 1978 है। इस संशोधन ने अनुच्छेद 30(1क) जोड़ा। संपत्ति के अधिकार को मौलिक अधिकारों से हटाए जाने के बाद यह प्रावधान सुनिश्चित करने के लिए लाया गया कि अल्पसंख्यक शैक्षणिक संस्थान की संपत्ति के अनिवार्य अधिग्रहण की राशि ऐसी न हो जिससे अनुच्छेद 30(1) के अधिकार का प्रभावी प्रयोग बाधित हो जाए।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (B) 44th Amendment Act, 1978

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: The 44th Constitutional Amendment Act of 1978 inserted Article 30(1A) into the Constitution. When the right to property was removed as a fundamental right, this amendment ensured that compulsory acquisition of property belonging to a minority educational institution requires state compensation at rates that do not restrict or abrogate the fundamental right guaranteed under Article 30(1) of the Constitution.

questions.question_hindi:
शैक्षणिक संवैधानिक कानून में निम्नलिखित विधिक सिद्धांतों और उनके अनुप्रयोगों के युग्मों पर विचार कीजिए:
I. मूल संरचना सिद्धांत: शिक्षा के अधिकार को गरिमापूर्ण जीवन के लिए आवश्यक मानने वाले तर्कों में इसका प्रयोग।
II. पृथक्करणीयता का सिद्धांत: किसी कानून के असंवैधानिक हिस्से को हटाकर शेष कानून को बनाए रखना।
III. असंगति (Repugnancy) का सिद्धांत: राज्य शिक्षा कानून और केंद्रीय शिक्षा कानून में टकराव होने पर प्रासंगिक।
कौन-से युग्म सही सुमेलित हैं?
questions.source: AI-generated from supplied reference material; Constitutional Provisions Related to Education
questions.subject: UPSC Principal Paper
questions.question_english:
Consider the following pairs of legal doctrines and their application to educational constitutional law:
I. Doctrine of Basic Structure: Applied in cases to argue that the Right to Education is essential to a dignified life.
II. Doctrine of Severability: Used to strike down unconstitutional parts of educational statutes while keeping the rest intact.
III. Doctrine of Repugnancy: Relevant when a State Education Act conflicts with a Central Education Act. Which pairs above are correctly matched?
questions.explanation_english: All three matches are legally accurate. Basic Structure applies to core rights including education; Severability isolates unconstitutional statutory clauses without invalidating entire Acts; and Repugnancy under Article 254 resolves operational conflicts between State and Central education legislation.
questions.explanation_hindi: सही उत्तर है: I, II और III। मूल संरचना सिद्धांत संविधान की आधारभूत विशेषताओं की रक्षा करता है; शिक्षा का अधिकार और गरिमापूर्ण जीवन से उसके संबंध पर संवैधानिक बहस में इसका उल्लेख हो सकता है। पृथक्करणीयता के सिद्धांत से न्यायालय कानून के असंवैधानिक हिस्से को अलग कर शेष को बचा सकता है। अनुच्छेद 254 के अंतर्गत असंगति का सिद्धांत समवर्ती सूची के विषय पर राज्य और केंद्रीय कानूनों के संघर्ष को सुलझाता है। अतः तीनों युग्म सही हैं।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (D) I, II and III

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: All three matches are legally accurate. Basic Structure applies to core rights including education; Severability isolates unconstitutional statutory clauses without invalidating entire Acts; and Repugnancy under Article 254 resolves operational conflicts between State and Central education legislation.

questions.question_english:
Consider the following Assertion (A) and Reason (R).
Assertion (A): The Fundamental Duty under Article 51A(k) is enforceable by a writ of Mandamus against parents who fail to send their children to school.
Reason (R): Fundamental Duties under Part IVA are non-justiciable in nature and cannot be enforced directly through court writs.
options_english: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false

questions.explanation_english: Fundamental Duties under Part IVA are nonjusticiable and cannot be directly enforced by courts through writs like Mandamus, making the assertion false. key_facts: Printed answer key: (D) A is false but R is true

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: Fundamental Duties under Part IVA are nonjusticiable and cannot be directly enforced by courts through writs like Mandamus, making the assertion false. questions.question_english:

I. It allows reservation in promotions if the State feels a backward class is inadequately represented.
II. It permits the carrying forward of unfilled reserved vacancies to subsequent years without capping the reservation limit at 50% for those carried-forward vacancies.

questions.explanation_english: Article 16(4A) permits reservation in promotions for SCs/STs inadequately represented in public employment. However, statement III is incorrect as reservations do not guarantee employment without meeting eligibility.
questions.explanation_hindi: सही उत्तर I और II है। पदोन्नति में आरक्षण का संवैधानिक आधार मुख्यतः अनुच्छेद 16(4क) से जुड़ा है, जो अपर्याप्त प्रतिनिधित्व की स्थिति में अनुसूचित जातियों और अनुसूचित जनजातियों के लिए व्यवस्था की अनुमति देता है। 81वें संशोधन से जोड़े गए अनुच्छेद 16(4ख) ने खाली आरक्षित रिक्तियों को आगे ले जाने के लिए अलग व्यवस्था दी। यह किसी भी पिछड़े वर्ग के प्रत्येक अभ्यर्थी को नौकरी की गारंटी नहीं देता, इसलिए कथन III गलत है।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (A) I and II

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: Article 16(4A) permits reservation in promotions for SCs/STs inadequately represented in public employment. The 81st Amendment inserted Article 16(4B), allowing unfilled reserved vacancies carried forward to be treated as a separate class, exempting backlogs from the 50% ceiling rule. However, statement III is incorrect as reservations do not guarantee employment without meeting eligibility.

questions.question_english:
Consider these statements regarding the Mohini Jain v. State of Karnataka (1992) judgment:
I. The Supreme Court ruled that the Right to Education is a Fundamental Right implicit in the Right to Life.
II. The judgment specifically struck down the practice of charging capitation fees by private educational institutions.
III. The Court limited the fundamental right to education only up to the age of 14 years. 
Which of the above statements are correct?
questions.explanation_english: In Mohini Jain v. State of Karnataka (1992), the Supreme Court ruled that the fundamental right to life under Article 21 includes the right to education, as dignity cannot be assured without it. The judgment held charging capitation fees in educational institutions illegal. However, it did not limit education to fourteen years; that specific age limit was later established in Unni Krishnan.
questions.explanation_hindi: सही उत्तर I और II है। मोहि‍नी जैन निर्णय में सर्वोच्च न्यायालय ने कहा कि अनुच्छेद 21 के अंतर्गत जीवन का अधिकार शिक्षा तक पहुँच को भी समाहित करता है, क्योंकि शिक्षा के बिना गरिमापूर्ण जीवन सुनिश्चित नहीं किया जा सकता। न्यायालय ने कैपिटेशन फीस की प्रथा को भी अस्वीकार किया। हालाँकि, शिक्षा के अधिकार को 14 वर्ष तक सीमित करने वाली विशिष्ट सीमा इस निर्णय में नहीं तय की गई थी; वह बाद के उन्नीकृष्णन निर्णय से जुड़ी थी।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (A) I and II

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: In Mohini Jain v. State of Karnataka (1992), the Supreme Court ruled that the fundamental right to life under Article 21 includes the right to education, as dignity cannot be assured without it. The judgment held charging capitation fees in educational institutions illegal. However, it did not limit education to fourteen years; that specific age limit was later established in Unni Krishnan.

I. Entry 63, 64, 65, and 66 of the Union List limit the scope of the State's power over education in the Concurrent List.

questions.question_english: The Supreme Court in the Champakam Dorairajan case (1951) held that in case of a conflict between Fundamental Rights and Directive Principles:
options_english: Both are equally important and must be harmonized.
questions.explanation_english: In State of Madras v. Champakam Dorairajan (1951), the Supreme Court ruled that Fundamental Rights under Part III take precedence over Directive Principles of State Policy under Part IV in case of conflict. The Court held that Directive Principles must run subsidiary to Fundamental Rights, leading to the 1st Constitutional Amendment.
questions.explanation_hindi: सही उत्तर A है। स्टेट ऑफ मद्रास बनाम चंपकम दोरैराजन (1951) में सर्वोच्च न्यायालय ने माना कि संविधान के भाग III में दिए गए मौलिक अधिकार, टकराव की स्थिति में, भाग IV के नीति-निदेशक तत्वों पर प्राथमिकता रखते हैं। इस निर्णय ने शिक्षा में आरक्षण-संबंधी नीति और संवैधानिक समानता के बीच संबंध पर महत्त्वपूर्ण प्रभाव डाला। बाद में संविधान संशोधनों ने राज्य को कुछ विशेष उपाय करने के लिए स्पष्ट सक्षम प्रावधान दिए।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (A) Fundamental Rights would prevail.

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: In State of Madras v. Champakam Dorairajan (1951), the Supreme Court ruled that Fundamental Rights under Part III take precedence over Directive Principles of State Policy under Part IV in case of conflict. The Court held that Directive Principles must run subsidiary to Fundamental Rights, leading to the 1st Constitutional Amendment.

questions.question_english:
Consider the following pairs of Articles and their core themes:
I. Article 15(4) - Special provision for socially and educationally backward classes.
II. Article 16(4) - Reservation in public employment.
III. Article 17 - Abolition of untouchability.
IV. Article 21A - Right to Education. 
How many pairs given above are correctly matched?
questions.explanation_english: All four pairs are correctly matched: Article 15(4) covers backward class provisions; Article 16(4) covers employment reservations; Article 17 abolishes untouchability; and Article 21A guarantees the right to education. Therefore, all four pairs represent accurate matches.

questions.question_english: Under Article 15(6), the State is empowered to make special provisions for the advancement of any economically weaker sections of citizens. What is the maximum percentage of reservation permitted under this clause in addition to the existing reservations?
questions.explanation_english: Article 15(6) explicitly specifies that reservations provided for Economically Weaker Sections (EWS) in educational institutions shall be subject to a maximum cap of ten percent. This 10% quota operates in addition to pre-existing reservations provided for SCs, STs, and Non-Creamy Layer OBCs under Article 15(4) and 15(5).
questions.explanation_hindi: सही उत्तर 10% है। अनुच्छेद 15(6) आर्थिक रूप से कमजोर वर्गों के लिए शैक्षणिक संस्थानों में अधिकतम दस प्रतिशत आरक्षण की अनुमति देता है। यह कोटा मौजूदा आरक्षण के अतिरिक्त है और संविधान तथा लागू कानूनों में निर्दिष्ट पात्रता, संस्थानों और अपवादों के अधीन है। इसलिए 5%, 15% या 27% को इस अनुच्छेद में निर्धारित अधिकतम सीमा बताना सही नहीं होगा।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (B) 10%

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: Article 15(6) explicitly specifies that reservations provided for Economically Weaker Sections (EWS) in educational institutions shall be subject to a maximum cap of ten percent. This 10% quota operates in addition to pre-existing reservations provided for SCs, STs, and Non-Creamy Layer OBCs under Article 15(4) and 15(5).

questions.question_english: Which Article of the Constitution states that "No religious instruction shall be provided in any educational institution wholly maintained out of State funds"?
questions.explanation_english: Article 28(1) explicitly states that no religious instruction shall be provided in any educational institution wholly maintained out of State funds. This provision enforces absolute state neutrality in government-funded educational institutions, ensuring public schools remain strictly secular environments free from mandatory religious teaching.
questions.explanation_hindi: सही उत्तर है: अनुच्छेद 28(1)। यह प्रावधान उन शैक्षणिक संस्थानों में धार्मिक शिक्षा दिए जाने पर रोक लगाता है जो पूरी तरह राज्य निधि से संचालित होते हैं। इसका उद्देश्य सार्वजनिक निधि से चलने वाले संस्थानों में धार्मिक तटस्थता बनाए रखना है। इसे अनुच्छेद 28(2) और 28(3) से अलग समझना चाहिए, जिनमें कुछ ट्रस्ट-आधारित संस्थानों तथा राज्य-मान्यता प्राप्त या सहायता प्राप्त संस्थानों में सहभागिता/सहमति से संबंधित अलग नियम हैं।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (D) Article 28(1)
